clue.text: Dark, stout hotel-worker on late shift

parts.note: the dark hours are the night
porter is a dark stout beer

explanation.surface: Someone describes a gloomy, portly man who works nights at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark, stout' reads as a description of a person; both words are really nouns for the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: This employee mans the hotel desk through the small hours, when the day staff have gone home.

clue.text: Springtime activity — some of the most earnest in Gravesend

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run across them

explanation.surface: A seasonal pastime is credited to the keenest people in a Kentish town.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside 'earnest', takes all of 'in' and the G of Gravesend, a town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds build homes for their eggs in spring, so this is a typical seasonal activity.

clue.text: Eat too much Cheddar, perhaps

definitions.meaning: Cheddar ... is a famous limestone ravine in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: Someone overindulges in cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar looks like the cheese, but here it is the English canyon the cheese is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is one sense; a steep rocky ravine, as at Cheddar in Somerset, is the other.

clue.text: Filling to the brim is super at university

parts.note: topping is old British slang for excellent
up means in residence at a university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: A student says a full glass at college is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Refilling a glass until it is completely full is to replenish it to the top.

clue.text: Unrestricted, presumably, this Scottish resort

parts.note: read as O (nothing) and BAN, the name says 'no ban', which is what unrestricted means

explanation.surface: A Scottish seaside town is assumed to have no rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presumably' admits the joke: split the town's name as zero plus ban, and it describes freedom from restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a port and holiday town on the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Evidence of a slack washer?

parts.note: a lazy person who washes carelessly leaves a dirty line on the neck, or a ring round the bath

explanation.definitionFit: A grimy line left on a bath or on unwashed skin shows the level the water reached.

clue.text: Crest of tail of bird given at Christmas

indicators.note: only the end portion of the bird's name is kept, its front part dropped

parts.note: a partridge in a pear tree is the first gift in the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone admires the feathered top of a festive bird's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crest' suggests a bird's plumage, fitting the surface, but it means a hilltop line.
explanation.definitionFit: A crest is the top line of a hill or wave, the same as its long raised top.

clue.text: Mistress who removed the locks?

parts.note: not a burglar but the biblical lover who had Samson's hair cut off, robbing him of his strength

explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Judges, Samson's lover betrayed him by having his hair shorn.

clue.text: Army formation in mathematical operation

definitions.meaning: a large military unit of several brigades
the arithmetic process of sharing one number by another

explanation.surface: Soldiers line up inside a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a large military unit and the arithmetic of sharing one number by another.

clue.text: Heaps of people are left in it

definitions.text: Heaps of people are left in it

parts.words: Heaps of people are left in it
parts.note: heaps here are old worn-out cars belonging to people, abandoned at a place for junk

explanation.definitionFit: Old wrecked cars, called heaps, are dumped at a place where metal is salvaged.

clue.text: Not well, going to doctor-that's the routine

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A sick person's regular visit to the GP.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a set procedure practised repeatedly, the established way of doing something.

clue.text: Soviet region does not begin to be favourite holiday peninsula

indicators.note: the region's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Siberia is the vast region of Russia, part of the Soviet Union

explanation.surface: A cold Russian territory is contrasted with a sunny vacation spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian peninsula, holding Spain and Portugal, is a popular destination for sun-seeking tourists.

clue.text: Akenhead goes in to endanger what belongs to the Empire

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as the surface's man enters

parts.note: to imperil is to put in danger
the head, or first letter, of the name Akenhead

explanation.surface: A man called Akenhead intrudes and threatens the imperial domain.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Akenhead carries its own signal: its head is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial describes anything pertaining to an empire or emperor.

clue.text: Where we go for air and spirit

definitions.text: Where we go for air and spirit

parts.words: Where we go for air and spirit
parts.note: not a holiday for fresh air and uplift, but a filling station for tyre air and motor spirit

explanation.definitionFit: A service station supplies air for tyres and petrol, once called motor spirit.

clue.text: Germaine, we hear, an aunt perhaps

definitions.meaning: the name sounds like germane, meaning pertinent or connected
an aunt is one example of a family member

explanation.surface: A woman named Germaine is rumoured to be someone's aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a sound-alike: Germaine is said like germane, which means pertinent, a sense of the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both pertinent or connected and a family member such as an aunt.

clue.text: Char, for example, wrapping steak like a dowdy woman

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second as packaging covers food

parts.note: char is a kind of fish related to trout
rump is a cut of steak

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady wraps up a piece of meat, looking drab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' suggests a British cleaning woman, a dowdy figure that fits the surface; here it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumpish means drab and unfashionable in dress, as an old-fashioned woman might be.

clue.text: Parisienne finds motorway eating-place

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, with the 1 read as I
a dinette is a small dining area

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman stops at a service-station café.
explanation.definitionFit: A midinette is a Parisian shop girl or seamstress, so a young woman of Paris.

clue.text: Integral form of percussion instrument

indicators.note: a new form or shape of the word's letters is made

explanation.surface: Something essential forms part of a drum kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel bar bent into a three-sided shape, struck with a rod, used in orchestras.

clue.text: Hotel rip-off, where they charge for egg-beaters!

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An overpriced hotel is compared to a place charging for whisks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rip-off' looks like one word, but 'off' is the anagram signal for HOTEL RIP. 'Egg-beaters' is slang for helicopters, and 'charge' means both bill and refuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing pad where helicopters, nicknamed egg-beaters, land and refuel.

clue.text: Principal method of making progress

parts.note: a head is a school principal
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A headteacher's chief technique for advancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward movement or advance toward a goal, as in making steady gains.

clue.text: A fellow is a handsome youth

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a certain man is good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this beautiful young man was loved by Aphrodite, so the name means any good-looking youth.

clue.text: English poet begins to speak and think in French

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: penser is French for to think

explanation.surface: A poet starts to talk and reflects in another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene in the Elizabethan age.

clue.text: As in rate of exchange as well?

indicators.note: exchanging the letters' places produces a new word

explanation.surface: A remark about the currency rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate of exchange' looks like a money phrase; 'of exchange' is the anagram signal for AS IN RATE, and the answer describes a type of well.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well taps water under pressure so it rises without pumping.

clue.text: Maytime has no name for spray of flowers

indicators.note: the season's name loses a letter

parts.note: May falls in spring, the season

explanation.surface: A nameless season is suited to a bunch of blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stem bearing leaves or blossoms, a little bouquet.

clue.text: Make a man of, say?

parts.note: not making someone grown-up, but turning a place into something like the Isle of Man, an island

explanation.definitionFit: To isolate as on an island; the Isle of Man is one such landmass.

clue.text: That lady takes record for silly things

parts.note: she refers to a woman
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A woman buys a disc for some foolish purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are proverbially foolish, followers who imitate one another.

clue.text: One in study leads chapter

definitions.meaning: a university official in charge of a faculty
the head of a cathedral's governing body, its chapter

explanation.surface: A scholar heads a section of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: It denotes both a college or faculty head and the senior cleric presiding over a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Woman, getting rave review, will become unsteady

indicators.note: to review is to look over again, so the letters are reconsidered and reordered

explanation.surface: A woman gets a glowing write-up but loses confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rave review' reads as high praise; 'review' is the anagram signal, turning RAVE into AVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To falter or wobble is to lose steadiness.

clue.text: People have this thrust upon them in sergeants'mess

definitions.text: People have this thrust upon them

indicators.note: making a mess of the letters jumbles them

explanation.surface: Someone is honoured with promotion in the army canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelfth Night's 'some have greatness thrust upon them'; 'mess' looks like the soldiers' dining hall but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line about eminence: some are born to it, some achieve it, some receive it.

clue.text: On course, does he retain the pot?

definitions.text: On course, does he retain the pot?

parts.words: On course, does he retain the pot?
parts.note: not a sports champion keeping a trophy, but the man on a golf course who looks after the putting surface and its hole

explanation.definitionFit: This groundsman tends the putting surface on a golf course.
